step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Bristol Myers Squibb's 'AutoPTP' (Automatic Promote to Production) DevOps pipeline factory. A deployment request is sent as a JSON descriptor through API Gateway to the Factory Lambda, which dynamically builds a Master CodePipeline. The Master CodePipeline coordinates approval checks with ServiceNow and triggers status/error notifications via a Notification Lambda to SES (Email Notification). It then orchestrates task executions across a Sub CodePipeline, CloudFormation, CodeBuild, and CodeDeploy.

graph.name: Bristol Myers Squibb AutoPTP DevOps Architecture
graph.notes: AutoPTP dynamic CodePipeline factory model for automated deployment management at scale.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point receiving deployment descriptor JSON requests via curl or web interface.

nodes.name: Factory Lambda
nodes.notes: Parses the deployment descriptor JSON and constructs the dynamic CodePipeline on the fly.

nodes.name: Master CodePipeline
nodes.notes: Master orchestration pipeline generated by the factory lambda to run deployment steps.

nodes.name: ServiceNow
nodes.notes: Integrates change management approval verification for production environments.

nodes.name: Notification Lambda
nodes.notes: Processes pipeline completion or failure status and prepares notification messages.

nodes.name: Email Notification
nodes.notes: Sends email updates with deployment outcomes or error details to developers.

nodes.name: Sub CodePipeline
nodes.notes: Sub-pipeline invoked for team-customized build/test actions.

nodes.name: CodeBuild
nodes.notes: Compiles and packages application code pay-as-you-go.

nodes.name: CodeDeploy
nodes.notes: Deploys application artifacts to target instances, Beanstalk, or on-premise servers.

edges.notes: Submits deployment descriptor JSON payload to the Factory Lambda.
